mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This relationship holds consistently across monetary policy cycles.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 4.5% (the 25th percentile of historical values), or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 3.6% (the 75th percentile of the 2020-2023 historical distribution) signals deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering a sell-off in equities and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 3.6%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A high federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%) combined with elevated inflation (CPIAUCSL > 300) signals a restrictive monetary policy stance amid persistent inflation, causing equity market sell-offs and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% and CPIAUCSL > 300, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of housing market contraction (HOUST < 1400), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced consumer spending and business investment linked to the housing sector.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 1400, or the Rank IC between HOUST and 20-day returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of total nonfarm employment (PAYEMS) indicates a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when PAYEMS is above the 75th percentile of historical values (155,000 thousand), or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is less than 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 102.0 (the 25th percentile of the 2020-2023 historical distribution) indicates a weakening manufacturing sector, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO < 102.0, or the Rank IC between INDPRO and 60-day returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer credit demand (RSAFS) is above 680,000 million dollars and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4.5%, the market perceives a high risk of debt distress and restrictive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS > 680000 and FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of weak economic growth (GDPC1 < 20000 billion dollars, the 25th percentile of the 2020-2023 historical distribution), the S&P 500 exhibits negative forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate lower corporate earnings and reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when GDPC1 < 20000, or the Rank IC between GDPC1 and 5-day returns is less than 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
